question.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157829/assets/4870d8e5469a2ccc429a0325a19a422820a65a145fa9651b55fe174b17e59841.svg) of $\mathbb R^2,$ find $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}$ if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157829/assets/4555a53bc8e10db083aca9cab2ffde97d414f86c5c90366da1b0ace1f82dad5d.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157829/assets/a7be5a62fbf433bf7c0e324aeb284a9c17cf31df39c2e8cc2a9bc1ace486dc98.svg) where $x_i = \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i.$ Computing the components of $\mathbf{x},$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-2-6=-8 \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-4+3=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157829/assets/da4ec39d0dbf73a9ec10828d14a2c2f3b0b2907a48e878f97b732d35b02d8200.svg)
